name: manual_df6827
claim: For claude.ai web/mobile agents working in an ephemeral bash sandbox (not a persistent local Claude Code CLI session): the sandbox filesystem can be wiped between turns without warning, mid-task, losing all uncommitted local work regardless of how much testing/verification was already done on it. This is not the same failure mode as a lost conversation -- the chat context and prior turns' summaries survive, but the actual git checkouts, installed tools (ripgrep, jq, etc.), and any uncommitted changes do not. Mitigation: commit AND push each logical, independently-tested unit of work as soon as it is complete and verified, rather than accumulating multiple fixes locally and pushing once at the end of a large task -- "push once at the end" is only safe advice for a session that won't lose its filesystem. When a reset is detected (home directory nearly empty, repo checkouts missing), re-clone fresh and re-verify everything from scratch rather than trusting the prior turn's summary of what was done -- installed tooling, test collection, and even file contents need re-confirming, not just re-stated. Re-use the same branch name across the pre-reset and post-reset work (on all affected repos, paired by name if the task spans repos) so recovery doesn't fragment one logical change into multiple disconnected branches. Do not relax RED-first TDD discipline during recovery to save time; re-verify each fix's test genuinely fails before the implementation exists, the same as before the reset -- speed pressure from lost work is not a reason to skip verification.

decisions.notes: Explicit user instruction to record this recovery strategy for future claude.ai agents in ephemeral-sandbox contexts (not persistent Claude Code CLI sessions), so they adopt incremental commit-and-push rather than repeat the same loss.
